old_problem: The row's titled intent is SMBIOS Port Connector Information, standardized as Type 8, while its literal command requests Type 14 Group Associations. These schemas have unrelated record fields, so the historical review correctly blocked any attempt to label one as the other. DeepSeek additionally imports Type 24 Hardware Security from Functionality row 1547 / variant 26410429a52657cb. The previous record assumed an owner had to select one branch, leaving both Pending and BLOCKED.
disposition_reason: Selection is unnecessary because both structures are safe read-only metadata and can be tested independently. Branch A preserves the title/intent by collecting every standard Type 8 Port Connector Information structure and comparing its five connector fields with the board connector matrix. Branch B preserves the literal Procedure by collecting every Type 14 Group Associations structure and comparing group names plus every member type/handle pair with the firmware group matrix. Neither branch cross-credits the other; Type 24 remains exclusively row 1547. Exact target matrices, optional/absent policy and parser version are bounded Project configuration. This full-source union removes the executable ambiguity and prior BLOCKED state without editing Master or losing coverage.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1543, same-row tests.json/DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, historical V3.1 BLOCKED record, generic script identity, same-code row 1547 Type 24 record and locked queue were read directly. The next formal queue identity was independently verified as row 1558 / variant e393414987f43e79.
DMTF SMBIOS DSP0134 v3.9.0 defines Port Connector Information as Type 8 and Group Associations as Type 14. A numeric type selector determines record layout, not merely a display label.

Type 8 contains Internal Reference Designator, Internal Connector Type, External Reference Designator, External Connector Type and Port Type. It is accepted only against an exact platform connector/port oracle and cannot be derived from Type 14 output.

Type 14 contains a Group Name followed by repeated member Item Type and Item Handle pairs. Every member handle must resolve to a structure of the declared type within the same captured SMBIOS table; it has no connector-designator or connector-type fields.

Both reads are non-mutating and have independent deterministic parsers, so testing the union is safer and more coverage-preserving than choosing a winner or guessing that the title/command is a copy error.

Type 8 and Type 14 applicability can differ. An expected zero/absence is acceptable only when the exact platform BIOS/SMBIOS specification says that structure or entry set is not implemented/applicable; an empty command, parser error or unsupported privilege cannot pass or confer N/A.

Use complete raw stdout/stderr/status and preferably a hash of the complete SMBIOS table. Grep labels or a generic script summary can hide multiple entries, broken string indexes, duplicate handles or unresolved group members.

The generic private `smbios_all_type` script may supplement collection only after content/provenance/hash validation and proof that it preserves both native types; otherwise direct supported dmidecode collection is the executable contract.
Functionality row 1547 independently owns Type 24 Hardware Security under the same display code. Its command/evidence cannot be inherited, and this row supplies it no credit.

ED-02/ED-21 preserve same-code variants; ED-03/ED-04/ED-22 make matrices/version bindings Project inputs; ED-15 requires evidence-backed N/A; ED-17/ED-19 preserve the function under test; ED-26 prohibits retry/substitution; ED-33/ED-35 preserve both conflicting source surfaces; ED-36 removes normal inputs from BLOCKED; ED-38 reserves the DUT verdict.

test_case.test_name: Independent SMBIOS Type 8 Port Connector and Type 14 Group Associations verification
test_case.purpose: Preserve and independently verify both source-defined scopes: all SMBIOS Type 8 Port Connector Information fields against the platform connector matrix and all literal Type 14 Group Associations names/member references against the platform group matrix, without Type 24 substitution or firmware mutation.
required_package: Exact SUT/board/revision, BIOS build and SMBIOS major/minor/entry-point identity; versioned DMTF DSP0134 interpretation and validated dmidecode/raw parser versions

Owner-approved Type 8 oracle for every connector: stable connector identity, internal/external reference designators, standard internal/external connector enums, port type and expected absence/duplicate/string-normalization policy

Owner-approved Type 14 oracle for every group: Group Name and ordered or explicitly unordered member list of standard Item Type plus Item Handle, including handle-resolution and duplicate/empty-group policy
Secure authenticated OS access with least-privilege SMBIOS read, protected raw/parsed evidence and hashes; optional private script content/hash/provenance approval only if used
test_case.test_command: READ-ONLY DUAL-SCHEMA COLLECTION; DO NOT EXECUTE DURING REVIEW. Bind Source Key/variant and capture exact target, BIOS, SMBIOS entry-point/table and parser/tool identities. Through protected access, execute privileged `dmidecode --type 8` and `dmidecode --type 14` as two separate commands with no grep or stderr suppression; record literal command, exit status, stdout, stderr, timestamp and evidence hash. Branch A: parse every Type 8 structure/handle and its Internal Reference Designator, Internal Connector Type, External Reference Designator, External Connector Type and Port Type; compare every field and expected entry with the board connector matrix. Branch B: parse every Type 14 handle, Group Name and every Item Type/Item Handle tuple; resolve each member handle against the same complete SMBIOS-table snapshot, verify declared type, group membership and all expected/extra/missing/duplicate entries against the group matrix. Report each branch independently, including authoritative expected-empty/N/A rules. Do not run Type 24, relabel a structure, clear logs or alter BIOS/ports/hardware. Use the private generic script only after proving its inspected version preserves complete native evidence for both branches.
test_case.expected_result: Every applicable expected Type 8 connector structure exists exactly as specified with correct internal/external designators, connector types and port type; every applicable Type 14 group exists with the correct Group Name and complete valid member type/handle set, and each handle resolves consistently in the same SMBIOS table. No unexpected, malformed, duplicate, dangling or cross-typed entries appear, expected absence is explicitly authorized, both commands complete cleanly, Type 24 is absent from this case and no platform state changes.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires exact target/BIOS/SMBIOS identity, complete successful raw Type 8 and Type 14 evidence, authoritative independent matrices, all structures/strings/enums/handles parsed, exact field/member matches and every Type 14 reference resolved to the declared native structure. FAIL covers a required present structure with missing/extra/duplicate/wrong fields, invalid enum/string index, dangling/wrong-type handle, malformed length/table or unexplained discrepancy. NOT READY covers missing matrix/tool/access/parser/script authority. Per-branch N/A or expected zero requires explicit platform specification. Type 14 cannot pass Type 8, Type 8 cannot pass Type 14, and row-1547 Type 24 cannot pass either. Tool Result remains separate from engineer verdict.
safety_gate: Both commands are read-only. Do not change BIOS, connectors, group membership, firmware, ports, hardware or logs to obtain expected output.
Use authenticated target access and least privilege; never expose passwords, disable host validation, suppress errors or accept empty/truncated output as successful evidence.
Preserve complete native structures, table identity, handles and parser versions. Never rename Type 14 as Port Connector, normalize Type 8 into group data or invoke Type 24 for this variant.
Validate the private script before use; a generic name, inaccessible contents or same-code association does not prove correct type selection or full-field coverage.

Stop on wrong target, concurrent BIOS update, malformed SMBIOS entry point/table, parse/version incompatibility or evidence-path failure. Preserve first output and do not automatically retry with filters or a different parser.
No physical connector test is implied: SMBIOS metadata correctness does not prove signal, link or mechanical functionality, which remains separate coverage.
The review agent executes no dmidecode/script/DUT action and issues no hardware PASS.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/variant, target/board/revision/BIOS/SMBIOS entry-point/table and dmidecode/parser identities; row-1547 Type 24 separation
Versioned Type 8 connector and Type 14 group/member expected matrices with per-branch applicability/absence policies
Literal commands, exit status, stderr, complete raw stdout/table hashes and every parsed Type 8 structure/field
Every parsed Type 14 group/member tuple, same-table handle/type resolution graph and invalid/dangling/duplicate diagnostics
Independent expected-versus-observed diffs and results for Type 8 and Type 14; private-script identity/coverage proof if used
No-mutation/no-log-clear audit, Tool Result/engineer-verdict separation and explicit no-DUT-action-by-review-agent statement
test_case.recovery: The workflow is read-only. On target, parser, table-integrity, handle-resolution or matrix ambiguity, stop interpretation, retain complete raw output/stderr/status and hashes, and close the protected session. Do not change BIOS/ports, run Type 24, substitute one schema, clear logs or rerun through a lossy filter. Resolve the table/parser/spec issue offline; a new collection requires a separately recorded attempt if the first evidence was incomplete.

source_conflict.reason: The incompatible title and command are no longer forced into one structure. Type 8 and Type 14 become distinct mandatory/applicability-governed checkpoints with native fields and evidence, preserving every source surface without equivalence or silent correction.

blocked.reason: Both native schemas, commands, acceptance matrices and safe recovery are now explicitly defined by DMTF. Exact platform expected inventories are bounded configuration; no unresolved command semantics or unsafe action remains.

external_authorities.title: DMTF SMBIOS Specification DSP0134 v3.9.0
external_authorities.application: Defines native Type 8 Port Connector Information fields and Type 14 Group Associations group/member structure, proving that both require separate collection and acceptance.

project_authority: The BIOS/platform owner supplies independent Type 8 connector and Type 14 group/member matrices plus applicability and parser policy; the engineer owns final verdict. They cannot relabel schemas, use Type 24/row 1547, allow one branch to cross-credit the other, accept empty/error output, waive handle resolution or treat SMBIOS metadata as physical connector function.
